zh: 重复在同一位置建墙不改变状态，所以每个位置只有“有墙/无墙”两种状态；查询只关心区间里墙的个数是否大于 0。
用树状数组（Fenwick 树）维护每个位置是否有墙：第一次建墙时把该位置加 1，查询时用两个前缀和之差得到区间内的墙数。
准备长度 n+1 的树状数组和一个“是否已建”标记数组；build i 时若未建过就标记并在 i 处加 1，已建过则什么也不做；query l r 计算 prefix(r+1) − prefix(l)，大于 0 输出 1，否则输出 0；所有查询结果按顺序用空格连接输出。
en: Building on the same position twice changes nothing, so every position is just "wall" or "no wall"; a query only asks whether the number of walls in the range is positive.
Keep a Fenwick tree over the positions: add 1 at a position the first time a wall is built there, and get the number of walls in a range as a difference of two prefix sums.

Keep a Fenwick tree of size n+1 and a "built" flag per position; for build i, if the flag is not set, set it and add 1 at i, otherwise do nothing; for query l r compute prefix(r+1) - prefix(l) and output 1 if it is positive, else 0; print all answers in order separated by spaces.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Use a Fenwick tree to record whether a wall has been built at each position. The first build at a position adds one there; a repeated build does not update anything. To query the closed interval [l,r], count its walls with the prefix sums prefix(r+1) - prefix(l).

## Correctness

Every built position contributes exactly one unit to the tree and every unbuilt position contributes zero; the idempotent update guarantees that repeated operations do not change any contribution. A Fenwick prefix sum returns the total contribution of the half-open range [0,x), so the difference of the two prefixes is exactly the number of walls in the closed interval [l,r]. That number is positive if and only if the interval contains a wall.

## Complexity

O(log n) time per operation, O(n) space.
